title: Applications for relief
subject: This guide addresses the process and requirements for making applications for relief under legislation administered by ASIC. It explains ASIC's general approach to granting relief, the types of relief available, and the fees charged for such applications.
background: ASIC has discretionary powers under various legislation to grant relief from certain legal requirements. This guide is intended for applicants and their advisers who seek relief, providing clarity on how ASIC will assess applications and the procedural steps involved. It was issued in February 2025, superseding previous versions from 2009 and 2006.
ruling: ASIC will consider each relief application on its merits, taking into account factors such as the purpose of the relevant legislation, the impact on stakeholders, and whether alternative mechanisms exist. Relief may be granted by legislative instrument (class relief) or individual relief, and ASIC may impose conditions. ASIC will not grant relief that would undermine the policy objectives of the legislation or that is contrary to the public interest. The guide outlines limits to the relief ASIC may grant, including that relief cannot override express prohibitions or requirements. ASIC encourages applicants to engage early and provide comprehensive information to facilitate assessment.
